articles.title: Alex Scott facing two months out after playing through pain with England
articles.summary: Midfielder’s thigh injury a blow for Bournemouth. He will miss England games on Tuesday and next month. Alex Scott has withdrawn from the England squad and could be out for two months with a thigh injury.
body: Bournemouth are unlikely to be delighted with how the situation has been handled, but Scott was determined to take his opportunity. He impressed alongside Elliot Anderson in Rijeka and was expected to be handed another start when England host Czechia in the Nations League on Tuesday. Thomas Tuchel will have to adjust his midfield for his side’s fourth and final game of the international break and for November’s games against Croatia and Spain.

Scott’s desire to represent his country was underlined by his decision to stay with the squad after the death of his grandfather. Declan Rice and Kobbie Mainoo withdrew at the start of the camp, meaning the replacements for Scott are James Garner and Myles Lewis-Skelly. Another solution would be to play Morgan Rogers or Jude Bellingham in a deeper position.

Tuchel, whose side are second in Nations League Group A3 and well placed to reach the quarter-finals in March, was delighted with Scott’s level against Croatia. The 23-year-old, who remains a key target for Chelsea, pushed on after a substitute appearance during last week’s win over Czechia in Prague.

articles.title: Czechia’s Santi Denia: ‘Anthony Gordon? What a player! He’s at the same level as Lamine Yamal’
articles.summary: After working with nearly all of Spain’s World Cup-winning squad in their formative years, the coach is also a huge fan of English football. He’s now pitting his wits against both.
body: A t the end of a 2-0 defeat by England in Prague, the Czechia coach turned left, walked along the touchline, shook Thomas Tuchel’s hand and said something he thinks he had never said at full-time: “See you soon.” To which Tuchel said back: “See you soon.” Seven days later, via Oviedo and Rijeka respectively, they meet again, at Wembley. “Four matches in 11 days, no time to train, for anything; I haven’t heard a single national coach say they like the new setup,” Santi Denia says, but it’s not all bad and there’s a big smile too.

This is the start of a new life, yet familiar faces await, warmth in every word. Very familiar faces. If Czechia’s opponents in this Nations League could not have been much worse, they could not have been much better either. In Oviedo, Denia’s team played his country, his players; in London, for the second time in a week, they play the nation he knows better than any other, more footballers he has seen grown up. Hello, again.

articles.title: A nation divided as Ronaldo left with big decision on Portugal future
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks at what could be the end of Cristiano Ronaldo's international career just days before the expected fanfare of Lionel Messi's Argentina goodbye.
body: As Lionel Messi prepares to get a hero's farewell for his successful international career, Cristiano Ronaldo's could have ended with him running down the tunnel at the final whistle of a game he did not play.
After the World Cup, Argentina's Messi, 39, decided to retire from international football, while Ronaldo, 41, opted to play on for Portugal.
Yet there is the possibility that Messi's Argentina career will end up lasting a few days longer - with a home friendly with Benin on Tuesday marked as his final game.
Ronaldo, furious at being made to warm up and not be brought on against Norway in the Nations League, walked out on the Portugal squad after finding out he would not start against Denmark either.

articles.title: How former Premier League goalkeeper David Stockdale rescued and revamped FC Farsley
articles.summary: Former Brighton and Birmingham stopper has his family getting their hands dirty rebooting Leeds club. They held a sweepstake in the FC Farsley office. How many fans would come for the first men’s game at their Throstle Nest ground in more than two years?
body: When 480 came through the gates to watch the all-new FC Farsley play Collegians FC in a Yorkshire Amateur League contest, Stockdale realised the scale of his achievement in getting the club back on their feet. There remains an enormous amount of work still to do – and Stockdale was operating a digger before this interview – but it was the first step of a fresh journey for the Leeds-based club.

The former Premier League goalkeeper, once of Birmingham, Brighton and Fulham among a host of other clubs, is aware his situation is abnormal. He never expected to be running a club when he took on the job of Farsley Celtic manager 19 months ago. By that stage, the club, playing in the National League North, owed about £750,000 in debts and was on the verge of being wound up.
“When I came in to help, I had no idea what had gone on,” Stockdale says. “I told them: ‘You’d better start telling me everything.’ They owed a lot of people money. This place was derelict.

articles.title: ICC delays plans for World Club Championship after ‘Big Three’ object
articles.summary: England, Australia and India say no space for extra events. No new international tournaments until 2031 at earliest. The International Cricket Council (ICC) will not introduce a World Club Championship or more international multilateral tournaments until 2031 at the earliest after resistance from…
body: After informal discussions between the ICC and member boards over several months, a cricket operations workshop in Dubai last week concluded without any additional events being proposed. This means the next addition of the Future Tours Programme (FTP) covering 2027 to 2031 will mirror that of the current cycle.

The one possible change to the next FTP is the expansion of the World Test Championship to 12 teams from next year, with the addition of Afghanistan, Ireland and Zimbabwe, although the ICC has yet to issue finalised plans to its members.

The ICC remains eager to explore new competitions as it seeks to grow the sport and its own revenues, which is likely to lead to tension with the so-called Big Three, although in reality India are out on their own as they generate around 70% of cricket’s global revenue.

The ICC is understood to have suggested a number of new concepts for discussion, including a World Club Championship and a series of four-team T20 competitions for international sides to take place during additional windows.

articles.title: England to play 50-over warm-up in stark Ashes contrast
articles.summary: England confirm warm-up fixture at the Waca before this winter's white-ball tour of Australia - a stark contrast to last year's Ashes defeat.
body: England will play a 50-over warm-up match against a Western Australia XI at the Waca in Perth before their white-ball tour of Australia later this year.
The confirmation comes after coach Brendon McCullum said last month he was hoping to arrange such fixtures to get players "up to speed" before next year's 50-over World Cup.

White-ball warm-up matches have faded from tours in recent years - England have not played one for six years - but this fixture is also a stark contrast to England's widely criticised schedule for last winter's Ashes series.
Before that contest, England played one in-house warm-up at club ground Lilac Hill. At the time, the England and Wales Cricket Board said they had been told the Waca was unavailable.

articles.title: £800m in, £800m out - Why Man City scandal shines light on Man Utd finances
articles.summary: Manchester City's owners have been found guilty of injecting money into the club. At Manchester United, fans are frustrated at how much has been taken out.
body: The Premier League panel's report laid it out in black and white.

In other words, Manchester City 's owners circumvented the league's financial regulations over a number of years by pumping money into the club that should not have been recorded as sponsorship income.
The damning judgement landed less than five days after Manchester United 's extended filing to the New York Stock Exchange which detailed their end of year accounts to 30 June 2026.
Contained within it was an interest payment of £37m, an increase from £34m the previous year.

articles.title: “That’s on Me”: Nick Sirianni Admits Costly Mistake in Eagles’ Collapse Against Rams
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles players had reasons to believe Sunday would end differently. Their defense intercepted Matthew Stafford twice, Darius Cooper caught two touchdown passes, and a 20-10 lead had Los Angeles running out of time at Lincoln Financial Field.
body: But the Eagles never found the play that would finish the game. Their advantage disappeared through a collection of failed conversions, penalties and missed tackles, leaving another loss that felt more self-inflicted than inevitable.

Philadelphia finished 0-for-12 on third down and converted only one of four fourth-down attempts. Those failures prevented the offense from building on the turnovers created by Cooper DeJean and Andrew Mukuba.

Jalen Hurts was stopped on a fourth-and-1 quarterback sneak during the third quarter. The more damaging failure came later, when Philadelphia faced fourth-and-goal from the Rams’ 2-yard line while leading 20-10.
Nick Sirianni kept his offense on the field instead of attempting a field goal. Hurts immediately faced pressure and threw off his back foot toward Cooper, but the pass fell incomplete.

articles.summary: Gareth Davies is to leave his role as chair of Commonwealth Games Wales (CGW) when his term ends in March 2027. The former Wales and British and Irish Lions rugby player took over as Team Wales chair in April 2023.
body: During his tenure, Davies oversaw Wales' preparations and involvement in the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games and the 2023 Commonwealth Youth Games in Trinidad and Tobago.
Non-executive director Wendy Barbour will join Davies in leaving Team Wales at the same time to end her 12-year stint.
Team Wales will seek new appointments to the roles with Davies playing his part "to ensure a smooth transition of board leadership".
"The organisation has been through a significant period of change and transformation," said Davies.

body: The Packers gave the ball away twice in the fourth quarter, leaving LaFleur clearly frustrated. He did not mince words when addressing the issue afterward, offering a harsh response to the repeated errors.
“I think a great teacher’s the bench. If guys don’t start holding onto the ball, they’re gonna be sitting on the bench,” stressed the Packers head coach.

Green Bay had a chance to create some breathing room late, but costly mistakes kept the Buccaneers within reach. MarShawn Lloyd lost possession following a 16-yard reception, although the fumble rolled out of bounds.

articles.summary: Northern Ireland's Glenn Irwin has been discharged from hospital after crashing in Sunday's British Superbike round at Donington Park. The 36-year-old was moved to Queen's Medical Centre in Nottingham after the incident because of "concern regarding a possible spinal fracture".
body: It said that Irwin been "pronounced clear and discharged and will be reviewed for fitness to ride at Brands Hatch".
Irwin crashed on the penultimate lap of the third BSB race of the weekend at Starkey's Bridge.
He was assessed and treated at the medial centre at the circuit, and was conscious and stable throughout.
It is the second time that the Ducati rider has been taken to hospital after a crash this season.

articles.title: McDermott explains Connor exclusion and England's World Cup game plan
articles.summary: Brian McDermott has consistently talked about England having a "point of difference" in the Rugby League World Cup but eyebrows were raised when the head coach opted to leave Jake Connor out of the squad again.
body: Connor was controversially left out of England's 3-0 Ashes drubbing last autumn by then head coach Shaun Wane and has once again had a strong season for Leeds Rhinos that led to his Dream Team inclusion.
However, McDermott has opted for George Williams, Harry Smith, and Mikey Lewis as his half-back options, with Sydney Roosters centre Hugo Savala also a capable half-back.
For McDermott, the players in that heavy Ashes defeat series were not the issue, but the game plan enforced that has been tried and failed many times before.

"It is not a case of changing players as such, although through the tournament we will pick the team that we think can best get the job done each week, but I believe last year that they didn't play with the points of difference," McDermott said.

articles.title: Messi lauded as Ronaldo involved in bitter dispute - a fitting finale?
articles.summary: Maybe it was inevitable, given how entwined their careers have been. But the comparison is irresistible. As Lionel Messi is lauded in Argentina during his farewell game, his great rival Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal career appears to be ending in acrimony.
body: As Lionel Messi awaits his farewell game for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo is embroiled in a bitter dispute with Portugal. Adam Bate looks at two careers entwined once more and wonders whether there is any way for Ronaldo to have his own satisfactory ending...

For Messi enthusiasts, the temptation is to conclude that it tells you everything about the two men. For Ronaldo's more vociferous fans, it is proof of a player not being given his due. Why is he not being afforded such status after doing so much for his country?

Ronaldo started the narrow win over Wales without scoring but was benched for the trip to Norway and was so frustrated by not coming on that he departed the camp. Portugal won that match and coach Jorge Jesus has followed it up with two more in his absence.

"I am not apologising to anyone," said Jesus in the aftermath. "If I need you for 30 minutes, you will play. If I don't need you, you won't play. No player will ever change my ideas as a coach. Not him, not any president, no one." It was not exactly placatory.
